translations.text: These are the words of the Teacher, the son of David, who reigned over Israel in Jerusalem.
“Emptiness upon emptiness is what exists,” said the Teacher. “Emptiness upon emptiness! Everything has emptiness within it.”
What profit does a person gain from all the toil at which he labors under the sun?
For one generation goes away and another comes in its place, but the earth remains forever.
The sun rises and sets, and draws back again to its own place, where it will rise.
It goes toward the south and turns, turning toward the north. The wind goes around and around and returns to its circuits.
All the flowing waters go into the sea, yet the sea is not filled by them. All the flowing waters return to their places, where they flow, to go there again.
All words are inadequate; a person cannot express them. The eye cannot be satisfied with seeing, and the ear cannot be satisfied with hearing.
What has happened? It is what will happen again. What has been made? It is what will be made again. There is nothing new under the sun.
A person may speak about things and say, “Look, this is new!” But they have already existed in the ages that came before us.
There is no remembrance of the earlier things, nor is there remembrance of the later things that came before us, or of those that will come afterward.
I, the Teacher, reigned over Israel in Jerusalem.

I devoted my heart to searching and investigating with wisdom everything that happened under heaven, for God has given human beings a troublesome occupation in which to occupy themselves with pleasure.
I saw all the things that had been made under the sun, and look, all of them contain emptiness and a desire of the spirit.
What is crooked cannot be put in order, and what is lacking cannot be brought into a count.
I spoke in my heart, saying, “Look, I have risen higher than those who were before me in Jerusalem.”
My heart experienced many things: wisdom and knowledge, parables and instruction. I understood them: look, this too is a desire of the spirit.
For great knowledge is found in an abundance of wisdom, and whoever adds to knowledge will add sorrow.
I said in my heart, “Come, let me test you with pleasure, and you will experience good things.” But look, this too is emptiness.
I called laughter bewilderment, and I said to pleasure, “What is this that you are doing?”

I considered whether my heart could entice my body as wine does, while my heart guided me with wisdom, and whether I could take hold of pleasure until I saw what was good for human beings to do under the sun during the numbered days of their lives.
I made my works great. I built houses for myself and planted vineyards for myself.
I made gardens and parks for myself, and planted every kind of fruit-bearing tree in them.
I made pools of water for myself to irrigate my grove of growing trees.
I acquired male and female slaves for myself, and I also had slaves born in the house. I had very large herds of cattle and flocks of sheep, more than all those who were before me in Jerusalem.
I gathered silver and gold for myself, and the treasures of kings and provinces. I acquired men and women who would sing to me in luxury with other people, and male and female wine servers.
And I became great and surpassed all who had been before me in Jerusalem, and my wisdom remained with me.
And whatever my eyes desired, I did not withhold from them. I did not deprive my heart of any pleasure, because my heart rejoiced in all my toil, and this became my share from all my toil.

And I turned again to all my works, which my own hands had made, and to the toil I had labored at to accomplish them. And look, everything was empty and a chasing after wind, and there was no gain under the sun.
And I looked to examine wisdom, madness, and foolishness. For who is the person who will come after the counsel, which is what they have carried out?
And I saw that wisdom has an advantage over foolishness, just as light has an advantage over darkness.
The wise person’s eyes are in his head, but the fool walks in darkness. And I too realized that the same fate will meet them all.

And I said in my heart, “What will happen to the fool will also happen to me. Why, then, did I become wise?” I said further in my heart, “This too is empty, because the fool speaks out of the abundance of his heart.”
For neither the wise person nor the fool is remembered forever, since in the days to come everything is forgotten. And how will the wise person die along with the fool?
And I hated my whole life, because the work done under the sun was evil to me, because everything is empty and a chasing after wind.
And I hated all my toil at which I labored under the sun, because I will leave it to the person who will come after me.
And who knows whether he will be wise or foolish? Yet he will rule over all the toil at which I labored and applied my mind under the sun. This too is empty.
And I turned to make my heart give up all the toil at which I had labored under the sun.

For there is a person whose toil belongs to him; there is a person who toils for himself with wisdom, knowledge, and strength. Yet there is a person who has not labored for it, to whom he will give his share. This too is empty and a great evil.
For it comes to a person in all his toil and in the desire of his heart, at which he labors under the sun.
For all his days are days of pain and anger, and a source of worry for him. Even at night his heart does not sleep. This too is empty.
There is nothing good for a person except to eat and drink and let himself see the good in his toil. This too I saw comes from the hand of God.
For who can eat and drink without him?

For to the person who is good in his sight, he has given wisdom, knowledge, and joy. But to the sinner he has given the troubling task of accumulating and gathering, so that he may give it to the person who is good in God's sight. This too is empty and a pursuit of wind.
There is a time for everyone, and a season for every activity under heaven.
A time to give birth and a time to die; a time to plant and a time to uproot what has been planted.
A time to kill and a time to heal; a time to tear down and a time to build.
A time to weep and a time to laugh; a time to mourn and a time to dance.
A time to throw stones away and a time to gather stones; a time to embrace and a time to refrain from embracing.
A time to search and a time to lose; a time to keep and a time to throw away.
A time to tear and a time to sew; a time to be silent and a time to speak.
A time to love and a time to hate; a time for war and a time for peace.
What, then, does a person gain from the work he labors at?
I saw all the work that God has given all people to occupy themselves with.
Everything he made is good in its own time. He has also placed all eternity in the human heart, so that a person cannot discover the work that God has done from beginning to end.
I understood that there is no good for them in these things except to rejoice and do good during their lives.
For everyone to eat and drink and enjoy good things in all his labor is a gift to him from God.
I understood that the things God has made will last forever. Nothing can be added to them, nor can anything be taken away. God made them so that people would fear him.
What has happened already exists, and the things appointed to happen have already happened. God will seek out what is being pursued.
I also saw under the sun that an ungodly person was in the place of judgment, and that a godly person was in the place of the righteous person.
And I said in my heart, “God will judge the righteous and the ungodly together. There is a time for every matter and for all the work.”
There I said in my heart, concerning what people say, “God will distinguish them and show them that they are animals.”

And what will befall people will not overtake them [?]. What will befall an animal will also befall them. As one dies, so the other dies, and the same breath is in them all. In what respect does a person have any advantage over an animal? None, because everything is empty.
Everything goes to one place. Everything came from the earth, and everything will return to the earth again.
And who knows whether the spirit of human beings will go up to heaven, and whether the spirit of an animal will go down to the earth?
And I saw that there is no good except for a person to rejoice in his work, because that is his share. For who will bring him to see what will happen after him?

And I turned and saw all the oppression that happened under the sun. Look at the tears of those who are oppressed: there is no one to comfort them. They are the ones who will be oppressed by force, and there is no one to comfort them.
And I praised all the dead, who had already died, more than the living, who are still alive now.
And better than both of them is the one who has not yet come into being, who has not seen all the evil work that has happened under the sun.
And I saw all the labor and all the skill in the work: a person's envy arises because of his neighbor. This too is empty, a craving for wind.
The fool folded his hands and ate his own flesh.
One handful of rest is better than two handfuls of labor with a craving for wind.
And I turned to futility under the sun.

There is a person who is alone, with no companion, and there is no end to all his labor. His eyes are never satisfied with wealth. “For whom, then, am I laboring, and why am I depriving myself of any enjoyment?” This too is empty, a miserable occupation.
Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their labor.
For if they fall, one will help his companion. But how unfortunate is the one who falls alone, with no second person to lift him up!
And again, if two lie down together, they will enjoy warmth. But how will one person keep warm alone?
And if one attacks, the two will stand against him. A cord of three strands will not break quickly.
A poor, wise child is better than an old, foolish king who no longer knows how to pay attention.
For he will come out of prison to become king; in his other kingdom he became poor.
I saw under the sun all the living who walk with this second youth [?], who will rise to take his place.
Is it not a distraction for the people, all those who came before him? And those who come afterward will not rejoice over him. This too is emptiness and a longing for wind.
Watch your step when you enter the house of God, and draw near to listen, for your sacrifice is better than what fools will offer, since they do not know how to do good.
Do not speak rashly with your mouth, and do not let your heart hurry to utter a word before God. For God is in heaven, but you are on earth. Therefore, let your words be few.
A dream comes through great trouble, and a fool’s voice comes through many words.
When you make a vow to God, do not delay fulfilling it, for there is no pleasure in fools. Fulfill whatever you vow.
It is better not to make a vow than to make a vow and not fulfill it.
Do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin, and do not say before God, “It was ignorance,” lest God become angry at your voice and destroy the work of your hands.
For amid many dreams, empty things, and many words, you must fear God.

If you see oppression inflicted on a poor person in a province, and justice and righteousness being taken away, do not be surprised at the matter. Guard yourself, being exalted in everything, and place yourself far above them on earth.
The king of the cultivated field is above everyone. Be faithful in everything. For the person who has been robbed, the matter is difficult.
Whoever loves silver will not be satisfied with silver. And who has been satisfied with the increase of his produce? This too is emptiness.
As enjoyment increases, those who consume it increase. And what strength comes from it? For the eye is the beginning of seeing.
Sleep is sweet to the servant, whether he eats little or much. But for the person filled with wealth, there is nothing that lets him sleep.
There is a sickness I have seen under the sun: wealth guarded by its owner to his own harm.
And that wealth will be lost through a harmful undertaking. He fathered a son, and there is nothing in his hand.
Just as he came naked from his mother’s womb, he will return and depart as he came. He will take nothing with him from his labor that he can carry in his hand.
This too is a terrible sickness: just as he came, so he will depart. And what gain has he obtained from toiling for the wind?
All his days are spent in darkness and sorrow, with great anger, sickness, and bitterness.

Here is the good that I have seen: it is good to eat and drink and enjoy all the labor at which a person toils under the sun, during the numbered days of his life that God has given him, for this is his share.
For everyone to whom God has given wealth and possessions, and the power to eat from them, receive his share, and rejoice in his labor—this is a gift from God.
For he will not remember much of the days of his life, because God keeps him occupied with the joy of his heart.
There is an evil I have seen under the sun, and it is great beneath heaven.

It is this: a person to whom God gives wealth, possessions, and honor, whose soul lacks nothing of all that he desires, yet God does not give him the power to enjoy it. Instead, a stranger will enjoy it. This is emptiness and a terrible sickness.

If a person fathers a hundred children and lives many years, so that the days of his years are many, but his soul is not satisfied with enjoyment, and he does not even receive a burial, I say that a stillborn child is better off than he is.
For it came in emptiness and will depart in darkness, and its name will be covered in the earth.
It has not seen the sun, nor has it known rest. This, then, is better than the other.
Even if they lived a thousand years on the roads, and he saw no enjoyment, will not all things go down to one place?
All a person's labor goes into his mouth, yet his appetite will not be satisfied.
For the wise person has an advantage over the fool, since the poor person knows how to walk before the living.
What the eyes see is better than wandering with one's desires. This too is meaningless and a longing of the spirit.
What has come into being has already been named, and it is known to be human. It will not contend in judgment with one stronger than itself.
For there are words that multiply meaningless things.

What advantage does a person have? And who knows what is good for a person in his life, or the number of days of his meaningless life, which he has spent like a shadow? For who will tell a person what will happen after him under the sun?
A name is better than oil or good mercy, and the day of death is better than the day of birth.
It is better to enter the house of mourning than to enter the house of drinking, because this is everyone's end, and the living person will take something good to heart.
Anger is better than laughter, for it will give him [?] in the heart of his face.
The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning, while the heart of fools is in the house of joy.
It is better to listen to a wise person's rebuke than to listen to the singing of fools.
Like the noise of thorns burning beneath a pot, so is the laughter of fools. This too is meaningless.
For slander will unsettle the wise person, and he will destroy the heart of his nobility.
The end of words is better than their beginning. A patient person is better than a proud spirit.
Do not be quick to become angry in your spirit, because anger rests in the bosom of fools.
Do not say, “Why did I come into being? The former days were better than these.” For you have not asked about this with wisdom.
And there is an advantage for those who see the sun.
For wisdom, when one is in its shade, is like the shade of money. And the knowledge of wisdom has an advantage: it will preserve the life of the person who belongs to it.
I have seen God's works, for who will be able to put in order what God will make crooked?
On the day of joy, seek what is good. On the day of trouble, look and consider this calmly. God made this for a reason, so that a person would find nothing after him.
I have seen everything in the days of my meaningless life. There is a righteous person who dies in his righteousness, and there is an ungodly person who lives on in his wickedness.
Do not be excessively righteous, and do not make yourself excessively wise, lest you ruin yourself.
Do not be excessively ungodly either, and do not be stubborn, so that you do not die before your time.
It is good for you to hold firmly to this, and do not [?] your hand from this. For those who fear God will have every good thing.
Wisdom will help the wise person more than ten people holding authority in a city.
For there is no righteous person on earth who does good and does not sin.
And do not pay attention to all the words that the ungodly say, so that you do not hear your servant cursing you.
For he will often act wickedly toward you, and your heart will often trouble you along your paths, because you yourself also curse others.
I tested all these things through wisdom, and I said, “I will become wiser.”
And it became very far from me, farther than it had been. And its depth was great. Who can reach it?
I set out, I and my heart, to understand, investigate, and seek wisdom and an explanation, and to understand the foolishness of the ungodly, toil, and madness.

And I found her, and I said, “More bitter than death is the woman who is a snare, whose heart is like nets, and who has a shackle in her hands. The person who is good in God's sight will be rescued from her, but the sinner will be caught by her.”
“Look, this is what I found,” said the Preacher, “adding one thing to another to find an explanation.”
This is what my soul sought but did not find. I found one man among a thousand, but I did not find a woman among all these.
But apart from these things, this is what I found: the human being whom God created, I found upright, but they sought many schemes. Who knows the wise, and who knows the explanation of a saying?
A person's wisdom will make his face shine, but the one whose face is shameless will be hated.
Pay attention to what the king says, and do not be hasty concerning an oath to God.
For you will go on your way. So do not persist in an evil matter.
Like a king who has authority, who will say to him, “What are you going to do?”
Whoever keeps the commandment will also know an evil matter, and the heart of the wise person will understand the time of judgment.
For everything has its time and its judgment, because a person's knowledge weighs heavily upon him.
For no one understands what will happen, and who will tell him how it will happen?

No person has authority over the spirit to restrain the spirit, and no one has authority over the day of death. There is no release on the day of battle, and wickedness will not save the person who belongs to it.
I saw all this, and I applied my heart to all the work done under the sun, in which one person took authority over another to harm him.
And then I saw the ungodly being brought into the tomb. They came out of the holy place and were honored in the city. This is how they acted. This, then, is futile.
For no objection will be raised by those who are quick to do evil. Therefore people's hearts are set on doing evil among themselves.
The one who sinned did evil from the beginning until their end. And I know that good will come to those who fear God, so that they stand in fear before him.
But no good will come to the ungodly, and the one who does not fear God will not prolong his days under the shadow.

There is something futile that has been done on earth: there are righteous people who receive what the deeds of the ungodly deserve, and there are ungodly people who receive what the deeds of the righteous deserve. And I said, “This too is futile.”

And I praised gold. There is nothing good for a person under the sun except to eat, drink, and enjoy himself, for this will be his in his toil during the days of his life that God has given him under the sun.
During these things I applied my heart to wisdom and to observing the occupation that takes place on earth, because neither by day nor by night will he see sleep with his eyes.

And I saw all God's works, and a person cannot discover the work that takes place under the sun. Even if a person exhausts himself searching, he will not find it. And whatever the wise man says he understands, he will not be able to discover it. For I laid all this upon my heart, and my heart saw all this:
How the righteous and the wise, along with their works, are in God's hands. Love and hatred are in everyone, but a person does not know them. Everything before them is futile.

One fate will overtake the righteous and the ungodly, the clean and the unclean, the good and the evil, the one who offers sacrifices and the one who does not. As it is with the good person, so it is with the sinner. As it is with the one who burns, so it is with the one who fears an oath.

This is an evil in everything under the sun: one fate will overtake everyone. The hearts of human beings are filled with evil, and madness is in their hearts during their lives, because they will go to the dead who are behind them.
For who will share in the company of all the living? There is hope for the living, for a living dog is better than a dead lion.
For the living will know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. There is no longer any reward for them, because their memory has been forgotten.
Their love, their hatred, and their jealousy have already perished. They will never again have a share in all the work done under the sun.
Come, eat your bread with joy and drink your wine with a happy heart, for God has approved your works.
Let your clothes always be bright, and do not leave [?].

And enjoy life with the wife you love throughout all the days of life given to you under the sun, throughout all your futile days. For this is your share in your life and in the toil at which you labor under the sun.
Whatever is ready at your hand to do, do it with all your strength, for there is no work, thought, knowledge, or wisdom in the realm of the dead, the place where you are going.

I turned and saw under the sun that the race does not belong to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, nor bread to the wise, nor wealth to the intelligent, nor favor to those with understanding. Their time and an unexpected event will overtake them all.
For a person does not know his time. Like fish caught in a good net, and like birds caught in a trap [?], so human beings will be caught in an evil time when it suddenly falls upon them.
And I saw this thing: I saw wisdom under the sun, and it was great in my eyes.
There is a small city with a small number of people in it, and a great king comes against it and builds great [?] against it.
And he finds a poor, wise man in it, and that man will save the city through his wisdom. Yet no one remembered that poor man.
Then I said, “Wisdom is better than strength, but the poor man's wisdom is despised, and his words are not heard.”
The words of the wise are heard in quiet, more than the shouting of those in authority [?].
Wisdom is better than weapons of war, and one person who sins will destroy much happiness.
When flying flies die, they spoil the perfumer’s preparation of oil. The word of wisdom is more highly valued than the day of great foolishness.
The wise man's heart is at his right hand, while the fools' heart is at his left.
And when a fool walks along a road, he will lack understanding, and everything he thinks about is foolishness.
If the spirit of someone in authority rises against you, do not give it room within you, for if you allow it, it will cause great sins within you.
There is an evil I saw under the sun, like a deliberate act coming from someone in authority:
The fool has been placed in very high positions, while the rich will sit in lowliness.
I saw slaves on horses, while rulers walked on the ground like slaves.
Whoever digs a pit will fall into it, and whoever tears down a wall will be bitten by a snake.
Whoever quarries stones will suffer pain from them, and whoever splits wood will be endangered by it.
If the iron becomes blunt and he has disturbed its surface, he will strengthen it with force. Wisdom, then, is a person's advantage.
If the snake bites with a whisper, there is no advantage for the charmer.
The words from a wise person's mouth are gracious, but a fool's lips will swallow him up.
The beginning of the words from his mouth is foolishness, and their end is an evil madness.
And the fool will multiply his words. A person does not know what has happened or what will happen. And who will tell him what is coming after him?
People's toil will wear him out—the one who does not know how to go to the city.
Woe to you, city, when your king is a little child and your rulers eat in the morning!
Blessed are you, land, when your king is the son of a free man and your rulers eat at the proper time for strength, and will not be put to shame.
Those who are idle will be brought low, and the house will leak because of the slackness of the hands.
They make bread while laughing, and oil and wine to make the living rejoice; and everything will obey money.

Do not curse the king even in your thoughts, and do not curse a rich person in the inner rooms of your bedrooms, for a bird of the sky will carry your voice, and a winged creature will repeat your words.
Cast your bread upon the surface of the water, for you will find it after many days.
Give a portion to seven, and also to eight, because you do not know what evil will happen on the earth.
If the clouds are filled with rain, they will pour it onto the earth. And if a tree falls toward the south or toward the north, it will remain in the place where it falls.
Whoever watches the winds will not sow seed, and whoever watches the clouds will not reap.

In these things there is no knowledge of the path of the spirit, just as you do not know the things inside the pregnant woman, that they are bones. In the same way, you will not know the works of your God, all the things he will do.
Sow your seed in the morning, and do not let your hand leave it in the evening, because you do not know which will succeed, this one or that one. And if both flourish, that is good.
Light is sweet, and it is good for the eyes to see the sun.
For if a person lives many years, he will rejoice in them all, and he will remember the days of darkness, because they will be many. Everything that is coming is emptiness.

Rejoice, young man, in your youth, and let your heart give you joy in the days of your youth. Walk in your ways without sin, and do not walk in arrogance or shamelessness. Know that for all these things God will bring you to judgment.
Let him remove anger from your heart, and let him remove evil from your flesh, because youth and ignorance are emptiness.
Remember the one who created you in the days of your youth, before the days of your misery come and the years reach you in which you will say, "I have no pleasure in them."
Before the sun and the light grow dark, along with the moon and the stars, and the clouds return after the rain.
On the day when those who guard the house tremble, and the strong men bend over, and those who grind stop because they have become few, and the women who look through a window grow dark.
And the doors to the marketplace are shut as the sound of those who grind grows faint; and they will rise at the sound of the sparrow, and all the daughters of blood will be brought low.

And they look up at the height, and fears arise on the road; and the almond tree will blossom, the locust will grow fat, and the caper plant will scatter. The mourners will lament in the marketplace, because the person has gone to his eternal home.
Before the silver’s appearance changes and the gold’s beauty is ruined, and the pitcher breaks at the spring, and the wheel [?] at the well,
and the dust returns to the earth as it was, and the spirit, in turn, returns to God, who gave it.
“What exists is emptiness upon emptiness,” says the Teacher. “Everything is empty.”
There is something more: the Teacher became wise and taught the people knowledge, and the ear will search for the meaning of the proverbs.
The Teacher searched for many years to find pleasing words and upright writing in words of truth.
The words of the wise are like goads for cattle and like firmly fixed nails, given through their companions by one shepherd.
Beyond these things, my son, be very careful not to make many books. There will be no end to them for you, and much study is wearisome to the body.
The conclusion of the matter is this: listen to it all. Fear God and keep his commandments, because this is the duty of every person.
For God will bring all creation before him to judge it concerning every deed that has been forgotten, whether good or evil.
